{
  "project_id": "P-UK-HyNetCCUSCluster",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Network capacity may be under‑utilised, reducing user fees and triggering reliance on the Revenue Support Agreement (RSA).",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure additional anchor or top‑up users early, include flexible capacity clauses and monitor utilisation to trigger alternative revenue sources.",
      "evidence": "Section 2.3.1 – risk of network underutilisation and revenue support exposure."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "CO₂ leakage from storage sites could cause environmental harm and trigger compensation claims.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Implement rigorous site characterisation, continuous monitoring, and rely on the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA) for high‑impact, low‑probability events.",
      "evidence": "Section 1.3 – government will underwrite CO₂ leakage risks via the SCA."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Construction cost overruns on the T&S network could exceed the allowed revenue cap.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply cost‑sharing caps (40% recovery beyond allowance), enforce strict procurement controls and regular cost reporting to Ofgem.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.1.3 – T&SCo will only recoup 40% of any costs in excess of the agreed level."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Discontinuation of the EETH hydrogen plant or Protos ERF would reduce CO₂ volumes and revenue.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Include performance milestones and termination penalties in contracts; maintain contingency users for the network.",
      "evidence": "Section 5.7.4 – Discontinuation risk for EETH and Protos."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Insufficient funds for de‑commissioning could leave a financial shortfall at end‑of‑life.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated de‑commissioning fund with regular contributions and escrow arrangements.",
      "evidence": "Section 5.7.5 – Decommissioning fund shortfall."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Cross‑chain risks between the T&SCo and capture projects may be poorly allocated, increasing overall project risk.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Allocate specific risks to the party best able to manage them via the commercial agreements and maintain a cross‑chain risk register.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.1.2 – government largely underwriting cross‑chain risks."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Regulatory changes or licence revocation by Ofgem could disrupt network operation.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Maintain close liaison with Ofgem, comply with the CCS Network Code, and monitor regulatory developments.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.4.2 – Ofgem as economic regulator with licence powers."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Non‑compliance with the Subsidy Control Act could lead to legal challenges or loss of funding.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Submit subsidy assessments to the Subsidy Advice Unit early and embed compliance checks in contract design.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.2.5 – Subsidy controls and legal requirements."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Delays in delivering the T&S network could push back the Commercial Operating Date (COD) of anchor projects.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Use phased delivery, buffer periods, and QSRA/PERT schedule assurance to monitor critical path activities.",
      "evidence": "Section 6.4.1 – overarching schedule risk to ensure timely COD."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Supply‑chain capacity constraints may cause construction delays and cost inflation.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Early engagement with key suppliers, secure long‑term contracts, and maintain contingency stock for critical materials.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.1.4 – cost escalation driven by supply‑chain cost increases."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Current low UK ETS carbon price makes capture uneconomic without subsidies, risking project viability.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide long‑term revenue support via RSA and CfD‑type contracts to bridge the price gap.",
      "evidence": "Section 1.1 – costs of capture higher than emitting due to low carbon price."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Potential fraud in subsidy payments could lead to financial loss and reputational damage.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement robust financial controls, regular audits, and fraud detection systems for all grant and subsidy flows.",
      "evidence": "Section 5.7.8 – Fraud."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Changes in government policy or funding envelope (NFE) could reduce available subsidies.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure multi‑year legislative commitments and embed flexibility in contracts to adjust to funding variations.",
      "evidence": "Section 5.2 – NFE of up to £20bn and reliance on exchequer funding."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Dense‑phase upgrade (Phase 2) may encounter technical challenges and higher than expected costs.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct detailed engineering studies, allocate contingency budget, and schedule upgrade after anchor COD to spread risk.",
      "evidence": "Section 2.3.2 – dense phase upgrades included in Phase 2."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Geological uncertainty could limit storage capacity or increase leakage risk.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Perform comprehensive site characterisation, modelling, and continuous monitoring of injection wells.",
      "evidence": "Section 1.1 – CO₂ stored in deep geological formations such as depleted fields or saline aquifers."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Long‑term RSA and SCA contracts may become unaffordable if cost assumptions change.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Include periodic review clauses, cost‑cap mechanisms, and shared‑risk provisions in the agreements.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.1.3 – RSA and SCA are 25‑year contracts providing revenue stability."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "If build‑out projects fail to take FID, the T&S network could become a stranded asset.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Tie network construction to firm user commitments, use the ‘uncertain cost reopener’ to limit CapEx exposure.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.2.2 – risk of network under‑utilisation if build‑out projects do not take FID."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "RAB model cost reopeners may lead to higher than forecasted payments to the T&SCo.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement rigorous cost monitoring, apply the 40% cost‑sharing rule, and conduct regular regulator reviews.",
      "evidence": "Section 5.1 – RAB model with cost reopeners settled ex post."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "Inadequate data management could impair performance monitoring and decision‑making.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop a comprehensive data‑management strategy, define data flows, and assign clear ownership for data quality.",
      "evidence": "Section 6.6 – data and information flows and data‑management strategy."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Network capacity may be under‑utilised, reducing user fees and triggering reliance on the Revenue Support Agreement (RSA).
risks.mitigation: Secure additional anchor or top‑up users early, include flexible capacity clauses and monitor utilisation to trigger alternative revenue sources.
risks.evidence: Section 2.3.1 – risk of network underutilisation and revenue support exposure.

risks.description: CO₂ leakage from storage sites could cause environmental harm and trigger compensation claims.
risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous site characterisation, continuous monitoring, and rely on the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA) for high‑impact, low‑probability events.
risks.evidence: Section 1.3 – government will underwrite CO₂ leakage risks via the SCA.

risks.description: Construction cost overruns on the T&S network could exceed the allowed revenue cap.
risks.mitigation: Apply cost‑sharing caps (40% recovery beyond allowance), enforce strict procurement controls and regular cost reporting to Ofgem.
risks.evidence: Section 4.1.3 – T&SCo will only recoup 40% of any costs in excess of the agreed level.

risks.description: Discontinuation of the EETH hydrogen plant or Protos ERF would reduce CO₂ volumes and revenue.
risks.mitigation: Include performance milestones and termination penalties in contracts; maintain contingency users for the network.
risks.evidence: Section 5.7.4 – Discontinuation risk for EETH and Protos.

risks.description: Insufficient funds for de‑commissioning could leave a financial shortfall at end‑of‑life.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated de‑commissioning fund with regular contributions and escrow arrangements.

risks.description: Cross‑chain risks between the T&SCo and capture projects may be poorly allocated, increasing overall project risk.
risks.mitigation: Allocate specific risks to the party best able to manage them via the commercial agreements and maintain a cross‑chain risk register.
risks.evidence: Section 4.1.2 – government largely underwriting cross‑chain risks.

risks.description: Regulatory changes or licence revocation by Ofgem could disrupt network operation.
risks.mitigation: Maintain close liaison with Ofgem, comply with the CCS Network Code, and monitor regulatory developments.
risks.evidence: Section 4.4.2 – Ofgem as economic regulator with licence powers.

risks.description: Non‑compliance with the Subsidy Control Act could lead to legal challenges or loss of funding.
risks.mitigation: Submit subsidy assessments to the Subsidy Advice Unit early and embed compliance checks in contract design.
risks.evidence: Section 4.2.5 – Subsidy controls and legal requirements.

risks.description: Delays in delivering the T&S network could push back the Commercial Operating Date (COD) of anchor projects.
risks.mitigation: Use phased delivery, buffer periods, and QSRA/PERT schedule assurance to monitor critical path activities.
risks.evidence: Section 6.4.1 – overarching schedule risk to ensure timely COD.

risks.description: Supply‑chain capacity constraints may cause construction delays and cost inflation.
risks.mitigation: Early engagement with key suppliers, secure long‑term contracts, and maintain contingency stock for critical materials.
risks.evidence: Section 4.1.4 – cost escalation driven by supply‑chain cost increases.

risks.description: Current low UK ETS carbon price makes capture uneconomic without subsidies, risking project viability.
risks.mitigation: Provide long‑term revenue support via RSA and CfD‑type contracts to bridge the price gap.
risks.evidence: Section 1.1 – costs of capture higher than emitting due to low carbon price.

risks.description: Potential fraud in subsidy payments could lead to financial loss and reputational damage.
risks.mitigation: Implement robust financial controls, regular audits, and fraud detection systems for all grant and subsidy flows.

risks.description: Changes in government policy or funding envelope (NFE) could reduce available subsidies.
risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year legislative commitments and embed flexibility in contracts to adjust to funding variations.
risks.evidence: Section 5.2 – NFE of up to £20bn and reliance on exchequer funding.

risks.description: Dense‑phase upgrade (Phase 2) may encounter technical challenges and higher than expected costs.
risks.mitigation: Conduct detailed engineering studies, allocate contingency budget, and schedule upgrade after anchor COD to spread risk.
risks.evidence: Section 2.3.2 – dense phase upgrades included in Phase 2.

risks.description: Geological uncertainty could limit storage capacity or increase leakage risk.
risks.mitigation: Perform comprehensive site characterisation, modelling, and continuous monitoring of injection wells.
risks.evidence: Section 1.1 – CO₂ stored in deep geological formations such as depleted fields or saline aquifers.

risks.description: Long‑term RSA and SCA contracts may become unaffordable if cost assumptions change.
risks.mitigation: Include periodic review clauses, cost‑cap mechanisms, and shared‑risk provisions in the agreements.
risks.evidence: Section 4.1.3 – RSA and SCA are 25‑year contracts providing revenue stability.

risks.description: If build‑out projects fail to take FID, the T&S network could become a stranded asset.
risks.mitigation: Tie network construction to firm user commitments, use the ‘uncertain cost reopener’ to limit CapEx exposure.
risks.evidence: Section 4.2.2 – risk of network under‑utilisation if build‑out projects do not take FID.

risks.description: RAB model cost reopeners may lead to higher than forecasted payments to the T&SCo.
risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous cost monitoring, apply the 40% cost‑sharing rule, and conduct regular regulator reviews.
risks.evidence: Section 5.1 – RAB model with cost reopeners settled ex post.

risks.description: Inadequate data management could impair performance monitoring and decision‑making.
risks.mitigation: Develop a comprehensive data‑management strategy, define data flows, and assign clear ownership for data quality.
risks.evidence: Section 6.6 – data and information flows and data‑management strategy.
